title: Complete local expansion of the availability function in random sequential adsorption of aligned squares at low density: Termination at fourth order
abstract: We consider random sequential adsorption (RSA) of aligned squares and derive the low-coverage expansion of the availability function alpha(q), the fraction of positions accessible to an additional square, up to fourth order in the coverage q. At low coverage, the reduction of available space can be understood in terms of geometric overlap between exclusion regions created by previously deposited squares. A single square blocks a finite area; pairs of squares may have overlapping exclusion zones, reducing the total blocked area; similarly, three and four squares can share a common overlap region, leading to higher-order corrections. These contributions can be systematically accounted for through an inclusion-exclusion expansion based on the geometry of overlapping exclusion regions, with alternating signs dictated by inclusion-exclusion. The expansion terminates exactly at fourth order, since no more than four deposited squares can simultaneously overlap the exclusion region of a trial insertion. The coefficients are obtained by explicit enumeration of all such geometrically admissible configurations and are further confirmed by numerical simulations on a discrete lattice, showing agreement within statistical uncertainty.
summary: This paper provides a detailed theoretical derivation for the low-density behavior of the availability function during Random Sequential Adsorption (RSA) of squares. By employing an inclusion-exclusion expansion based on geometric overlaps, the authors derive the polynomial coefficients up to fourth order. The work is significant because it establishes the exact local overlap hierarchy for this physical process and validates its results against numerical simulations.
main_problem: The authors derive the low-coverage expansion of the availability function, $\alpha(q)$, for Random Sequential Adsorption (RSA) of aligned squares.
main_result: They establish that this local overlap hierarchy terminates exactly at fourth order due to geometric constraints, yielding a complete polynomial approximation for low densities.
method: The derivation systematically uses the inclusion-exclusion principle applied to the overlapping exclusion regions created by deposited squares.
model_or_system: The model is Random Sequential Adsorption (RSA) of aligned squares on a surface or lattice. The process is irreversible, leading to a jammed state characterized by coverage $q$.
key_observables: The availability function $\alpha(q)$, which measures the fraction of positions available for an additional square insertion.
important_parameters: Low-density regime (low coverage $q$), and the geometric overlap structure involving up to four squares.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the low-density limit, assuming that only local overlaps (up to four bodies) contribute significantly to the expansion coefficients.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the exclusion zone of a single square and show how the overlap regions for two and three squares are geometrically accounted for in the inclusion-exclusion corrections.
paper_structure: The paper builds the expansion $\alpha(q)$ term by term, starting with the first order (single block), then systematically correcting for double overlaps ($C_2$), triple overlaps ($C_3$), and finally confirming the termination at fourth order ($C_4$) using both analytical geometry and numerical simulation.
why_interesting: While focused on classical packing problems, the rigorous application of inclusion-exclusion principles to calculate system properties based on local geometric constraints is a powerful technique applicable to understanding correlation functions in many-body quantum systems or open quantum dynamics where local approximations are used.
